title: Security posture discovery - NexaHealth
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
next_steps: Liam to send SOC 2 report + security whitepaper
Priya to propose initial benchmark plan for dedicated pilot
Schedule technical deep dive with Nexa infra team next week
David to share current data residency and retention policy docs
action_items: Liam Carter: Share SOC2 report and security whitepaper (due: 2026-09-22)
Priya Shah: Draft pilot benchmark plan and required test data (due: 2026-09-25)

Laura Park: Provide list of internal stakeholders for SSO/SCIM integration (due: 2026-09-21)
summary: Discovery with NexaHealth focused on security posture for potential Redwood deployment. Key concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC controls, audit log retention, envelope encryption and KMS integration, and data residency. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) for PHI-sensitive workflows. Agreed to send compliance artifacts and schedule an infra deep dive + benchmark plan.
transcript:
00:00:02 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): All right thanks everyone for joining, I'm Liam from Redwood. Quick roll call?
00:00:10 Maria Gomez (NexaHealth VP Eng): Maria here, David, Laura, Samir on my side.
00:00:15 David Chen (NexaHealth Head Sec): David here.
00:00:18 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood infra. Hey all.
00:00:22 Samir Patel (NexaHealth CTO): Samir here. Sorry for the delay.
00:00:30 Liam: No worries. Purpose of call is to run through security posture questions around using Redwood hosted/dedicated/private. We sent a short questionnaire earlier - David you had specific concerns about PHI and retention?
00:00:45 David: Yeah quick summary - Nexa handles PHI for our remote monitoring product. We need to know what evidence you have for SOC2/ISO, SSO integration options, RBAC granularity, audit logging of API calls, encryption at rest + KMS, and whether data can be kept in our region. Also curious on dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for compliance.
00:01:10 Liam: Great. High level: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and we're in process of pursuing ISO 27001, we can share the SOC2 report under an NDA - I'll drop it after the call. For ISO we have an attestation timeline, Priya can expand.
00:01:28 Priya: Yep. We run regular audits, our hosted control plane is multi-tenant but logically separated; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and network isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control of network boundaries. For PHI workloads many customers move to Dedicated or Private to satisfy contractual requirements.
00:01:50 Maria: When you say network isolation for Dedicated, is that customer VPC peering or is it within your infra? We have strict egress controls.
00:02:00 Priya: For Dedicated we support private peering into a customer VPC in supported clouds, and we can restrict egress and provide NAT/firewall rules. For Private deployment we ship a control plane that the customer runs in their VPC or air-gapped environment - that gives you full egress control.
00:02:20 David: And for encryption, how do you manage KMS keys? Do we bring our own key?
00:02:25 Priya: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM for Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption with our KMS but we also offer BYOK for enterprise plans and Dedicated. We'll provide integration docs.
00:02:40 Laura: What's logged? We need audit trails for API usage tied to user identities - not just a token.
00:02:46 Priya: We capture token-level metadata, request and response metadata, model and route, timestamps, and associated account and user IDs when SSO is linked. Audit logs are stored in an immutable store and can be exported to customer SIEMs. Retention policy is configurable per account, and we can set long-term archival for enterprise.
00:03:05 David: Is the log integrity verifiable - e.g., append-only or signed?
00:03:10 Priya: Currently logs are append-only with immutable storage and checksums; for Private we can integrate with customer signing or SIEM ingestion to meet stricter requirements.
00:03:20 Liam: To add - we maintain RBAC with roles and granular permissions per route and model. You can map SAML groups to roles via SCIM provisioning.
00:03:30 Maria: SCIM is important. Can we auto-provision groups from Okta?
00:03:34 Priya: Yes Okta, Azure AD supported. SCIM provisioning maps to RBAC groups, and session length and session revocation can be controlled via SAML assertions and our token settings.
00:03:48 Samir: For data residency, we need all PHI to remain in us-east-1 and stored for at most seven years with secure deletion on request. Is that supported?
00:04:00 Priya: We have region pinning for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can select region-backed endpoints for storage in supported regions. We can support retention windows and delete schedules; secure deletion depends on storage tier, but for Dedicated/Private you get stronger guarantees. We'll need to review contractual language for the 7-year retention and deletion SLA.
00:04:20 David: What about SSO session revocation if someone leaves the company - I need immediate token invalidation.
00:04:26 Priya: We support immediate deprovisioning via SCIM and SAML session invalidation. In addition tokens are short-lived and we support session revocation hooks to invalidate long-running sessions. For API keys we can rotate keys and revoke at user level.
00:04:45 Liam: On hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs - hosted is simplest but a shared control plane, though we offer strict tenant isolation and SOC2. Dedicated gives network isolation and reserved capacity, useful for predictable throughput. Private is for regulated or air-gapped needs. Cost/complexity increases respectively.
00:05:05 Maria: On backups and retention, is backup encryption tied to the same KMS? Do you run automated backups across regions?
00:05:14 Priya: Backups are encrypted using CMK if provided; cross-region backups only occur if you enable redundancy - for PHI customers we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with controlled failover policies.
00:05:30 David: Any external pen testing history and when last?
00:05:34 Priya: We do quarterly internal and annual external penetration tests; reports can be shared under NDA. Last external pentest was Q2 2026.
00:05:45 Laura: For the audit logs export, which SIEMs do you integrate with? We use Splunk and Sumo.
00:05:52 Priya: Splunk, Datadog, Sumo Logic and we also support S3/GCS exports and Kafka streaming for high-throughput customers.
00:06:00 Samir: What's the least-privilege model? Can we limit models/users to routes and max token quotas?
00:06:07 Priya: Yes per-role policies can restrict model selection, per-route limits, max tokens and rate limiting. You can also enforce canary rollouts so only certain groups get access to new model variants.
00:06:20 David: About data used for model tuning - do you ever use customer prompts or outputs to train models?
00:06:26 Liam: By default we do not use customer data to train public models. For hosted customers we offer opt-in data usage for improvement; for enterprise Dedicated and Private, data is isolated and not used. We'll provide the data usage agreement text.
00:06:40 Maria: Great. We'll need SOC2 evidence and the data usage clauses in the contract.
00:06:45 Liam: We'll send both. Also, Priya suggested a pilot: dedicated reserved pool with a small benchmark to validate latency and egress rules - do you want to do that?
00:06:55 Samir: Yes, pilot makes sense. We'll need an infra deep dive to confirm network flows and a list of test scenarios.
00:07:05 Priya: I'll put together a benchmark plan covering latency SLOs, KV cache behavior, and prefix caching, plus a checklist for KMS integration.
00:07:15 David: How long does it take to provision a dedicated environment?
00:07:19 Priya: Typical provisioning is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and network peering. Private deployments vary more - 4-8 weeks for on-prem or air-gapped.
00:07:30 Maria: Any compliance packages for HITRUST or HIPAA specifically?
00:07:34 Liam: We have HIPAA addendum templates and work with customers on BAA; HITRUST is not out-of-box but we can discuss controls mapping.
00:07:45 Laura: On key rotation, what's the cadence and are rotations seamless?
00:07:48 Priya: We support key rotation via KMS with zero-downtime rotations for most storage layers; you'll be able to rotate CMKs and we can coordinate for Private.
00:07:58 Samir: Ok let's recap next steps.
00:08:02 Liam: Recap: Liam to send SOC2 + security whitepaper, Priya to draft benchmark/pilot plan, David to share retention requirements, Laura to provide SSO stakeholders. We'll schedule a technical deep dive next week. Anything else?
00:08:15 David: Can you also include pricing ballpark for Dedicated so we can evaluate budget?
00:08:19 Liam: Yep we'll include a high-level pricing estimate and options.
00:08:23 Maria: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the detail.
00:08:26 Liam: Thanks all - we'll follow up with artifacts.
00:08:30 [call ends]
